steps.body: An angle's size is measured in **degrees.** A full turn all the way around is **360°.** Cut that turn exactly in half, and you get a **straight angle: 180°.** Cut it in half again, and you get a **right angle: 90°** — the same halving idea from fractions, now measuring a turn instead of a pizza.

widget.prompt: Slide to show a full turn — all the way around.
widget.lowFeedback: Keep sliding — a full turn goes all the way around back to where it started.
widget.highFeedback: That's past a full turn — 360° is as far as one full turn goes.
widget.successFeedback: 360° — one complete turn, all the way around.

predict.prompt: You'll slide all the way around to a full turn. How many quarter turns of 90° fit inside it?
predict.reveal: A full turn is four 90° corners stacked together — 90, 180, 270, 360. Four quarters make the whole spin.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents degree measurement.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for degree measurement must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines degree measurement.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: A complete turn all the way around measures 360°.
360° is the benchmark for one full rotation.

widget.prompt: How many degrees are in a full turn?

commonErrors.feedback: 180° is a straight angle — HALF a turn. A full turn all the way around is 360°.
90° is a right angle — a QUARTER turn. A full turn all the way around is 360°.

widget.fallbackFeedback: A full turn all the way around is 360°.

steps.body: The halving keeps going. Half of a right angle (90°) is **45°** — the diagonal angle you'd see cutting a square corner exactly in two. Same fraction-halving move, one more step down.

explanationVariants: Half of 90° is 45° — cutting the right angle exactly in two.

widget.prompt: What is half of a right angle (90°), in degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: 90° is the WHOLE right angle. Half of it is 90÷2=45°.
180° is DOUBLE a right angle, not half. Half of 90° is 45°.

widget.lowFeedback: Keep sliding higher — 45° is more than a small nudge past 0.
widget.highFeedback: That's past 45° — slide back down a bit.
widget.successFeedback: 45° — exactly half of a right angle.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents degree measurement.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for degree measurement must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines degree measurement.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: 45° sits between 0° and 90° — smaller than a right angle, bigger than nothing.
It's exactly halfway between 0° and the right-angle benchmark.

widget.prompt: Is a 45° angle smaller or larger than a right angle?

options.label: Smaller — 45° is half of the 90° right angle
options.feedback: 45° is exactly half of 90° — smaller than a right angle.

options.label: Larger — 45 is a bigger-sounding number
options.feedback: The number of degrees decides size directly: 45 is less than 90, so it's smaller, not larger.

options.label: The same — both are common angles
options.feedback: Common doesn't mean equal. 45° and 90° are different sizes — 45° is half of 90°.

options.label: Can't compare without a protractor
options.feedback: The degree numbers alone settle it: 45 is less than 90, so 45° is the smaller angle.

hints: A door opened all the way to make an L-shape with the wall is a right angle.
This door opens only halfway to that.
explanationVariants: A door making an L-shape (a right angle) is 90°. Opening only halfway to that is half of 90°, which is 45°.
Halfway to a right angle is 45°.

widget.prompt: A door opened all the way to form an L-shape with the wall makes a right angle. If this door is open only HALFWAY to that point, how many degrees is it open?

commonErrors.feedback: 90° is the FULL right angle (the door open all the way to the L-shape). Halfway to that is half of 90: 45°.
180° would be the door folded flat against the wall — far more than halfway. Halfway to a 90° right angle is 45°.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Halfway to a 90° right angle is 90÷2.

takeaways: A full turn is 360°; half of that is a straight angle, 180°.
Half of a straight angle is a right angle, 90°.
Half of a right angle is 45° — the same halving move as fractions, one level deeper.
steps.teaser: next: reading any angle's exact measure, using clock positions as a guide.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **A full turn is 360°.** Half of that is a straight angle (180°). Half of THAT is a right angle (90°). Each step just halves the one before it — the same halving move you already know from fractions.

explanationVariants: Half of 360° is 180° — a straight angle.

widget.prompt: What is half of a full turn (360°)?

options.feedback: 90° is half of 180°, not half of 360°. Half of 360 is 180.
That's the WHOLE turn, not half of it. Half of 360 is 180.
